subject: Post-demo: procurement readiness & preferred payment path
messages:
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Jensen <ajensen@oakridge.ai>, Emily Shaw <emily.shaw@oakridge.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 20 Nov 2026 15:12:00 -0800
Subject: Post-demo recap + quick procurement questions

Thanks again for your time today — appreciate the candid discussion about latency targets and the expected Q1 volume. Quick recap and two procurement questions so we can align next steps: 

Recap
- Oakridge target: integrate Redwood inference for customer-facing summarization (3M tokens/mo initial).
- Latency budget: p95 < 350ms for 512-token responses; burst tolerance required for peak hours.

Procurement questions (to help route you to the right commercial path)
1) Preferred payment method: do you want to purchase via card, PO, or through AWS Marketplace?
2) Any internal security gating beyond SOC 2 Type II and a signed DPA? (e.g., full questionnaire, pentest report, vendor risk tool)

Attachments: I attached a short SOC 2 summary and a draft DPA we typically start with for enterprise pilots.

Proposed next steps
- If you prefer PO or contracting, we can loop legal and send a short SOW + quote.
- If Marketplace is preferred, we can provide a SKU and procurement quick-start checklist.

Happy to hop on a 20-min call next week if that helps decisioning.

Best,
Kimberly Park
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
kimberly.park@redwood.ai
+1 (415) 555-0123

Subject: Re: Post-demo recap + quick procurement questions

Thanks, Kimberly — good summary. Short answers from our side: 

- Payment: Procurement prefers PO for anything above $25k ARR, and they like to use our internal contract templates.
- Marketplace: Finance would rather avoid Marketplace for now because of invoicing cadence. Not ruled out long-term but not preferred for initial pilot.
- Security gating: SOC 2 Type II report + executed DPA are mandatory. Additionally, our vendor risk team may request a completed security questionnaire (we use Shared Assessments) if the engagement hits production (which we expect in Q2).

Emily from procurement is cc'd — she will coordinate purchase timing and send the PO process document. For timing, we're aiming to finalize procurement by mid-December.

Regards,
Alex Jensen
VP Product, Oakridge AI
ajensen@oakridge.ai

Hi Kimberly — adding a couple of specifics from procurement: 

- PO cadence: We issue POs monthly. For pilots we typically do a 3-month PO and then convert to a longer-term agreement if metrics look good.
- Contract redlines: Please send your standard SOW + DPA; our legal will redline.
- Approvals: PR/PO needs manager + finance sign-off; that could take up to 10 business days once the SOW is final.

Can you send the SOW template and a concise quote that maps to a 3-month pilot? If you can highlight cancellation terms and data retention in the DPA, that will speed our review.

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Fwd: Post-demo recap + quick procurement questions

Thanks for the context. Quick points: 

- PO for a 3-month pilot: doable. For hosted usage we can accept PO with net-30. No minimum beyond pilot economics — we typically recommend a 3-month pilot with an estimate line-item and a cap on spend for safety.
- Pilot pricing: ballpark for 3M tokens/mo (mixed generation/embeddings) — $18k/mo. I'll produce a short quote that maps to their expected volumes and includes a 10% buffer option.
- SOW: include onboarding (2 days of onboarding support), a single-trace integration pass, and 30-day reduced-latency monitoring for p95 metrics. Also include a knowledge-transfer session.
- Security gating: SOC 2 Type II summary is fine to start; if Oakridge asks for the full SOC 2 report we can route via our security portal. For Shared Assessments questionnaire requests, we typically ask for the questionnaire file and then furnish evidence and a point of contact in Security. That process takes around 7–14 business days depending on scope.

I'll attach the SOW template and a short quote draft for Kimberly to send. If Procurement insists on contract redlines, we should be ready with a migration path to Marketplace later if they want a simpler procurement route.

Ben Carter
Director, Commercial Operations, Redwood Inference
